data.narrative:
Summit Lithium Technologies is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Amanda Hall that has raised approximately $120M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises nine comparable firms—one public (Linacore, LNZA) and eight private entities including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $120M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression. This approach yields an implied valuation of $240M. A peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied because the Climate & Energy comparable set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting narrow filtering criteria—only eight private companies exist in the sector overall, with insufficient clustering at Summit's stage to generate a statistically defensible median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $204M to $276M, with a central estimate of $240M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for this subsector, the absence of direct peer benchmarks at Series A, and the limited depth of comparable transaction data in frontier lithium-focused technologies. Any revision would require either documented precedent at this stage or access to a broader set of Climate & Energy Series A financings.
